idiom_name: Bunny Queue#subscribe block (or subscribe_with a consumer object)
implementation_notes: Bunny is the standard Ruby AMQP client: queue.subscribe(block: false) { |delivery_info, properties, body| ... } registers a block that Bunny's reader thread invokes per delivery - the RabbitMQ tutorial states the client pushes messages asynchronously to the callback - and subscribe_with(consumer) is the object form when you need state. The block or consumer replaces the classic listener object and no receive loop appears in application code; the manual fallback is Thread plus a Queue if you must build the endpoint yourself.
code_sketch:
queue = channel.queue("orders", durable: true)
queue.subscribe(block: false, manual_ack: true) do |info, _props, body|
  begin
    handle(JSON.parse(body))              # Bunny's reader thread invokes us
    channel.acknowledge(info.delivery_tag, false)
  rescue => e
    warn "rejecting delivery: #{e}"
    channel.reject(info.delivery_tag, false)   # dead-letter; no requeue
  end
end
pitfalls: The subscription block and your acknowledgements run on Bunny's reader thread; blocking or raising there stalls or terminates delivery for every consumer on the connection.
With manual_ack: true a crash before the ack redelivers the message - acknowledge only after the work, using the delivery tag from the callback.
reject with requeue=false (or ack) for poison messages; requeue=true spins forever on the same message.
subscribe(block: true) pins the calling thread (the tutorial uses it only to keep the script alive); in server processes prefer block: false with a supervised consumer.
